}}</ref> He also drew praise in the media for his ball control<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sportacademy/hi/sa/football/video_masterclasses/newsid_3532000/3532995.stm |title=Improve your control with Becks |date=12 October 2004 |work=BBC Sport |access-date=2 April 2020 |archive-date=15 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210415063104/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sportacademy/hi/sa/football/video_masterclasses/newsid_3532000/3532995.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> and ability to create space for himself on the pitch,<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sportacademy/hi/sa/football/video_masterclasses/newsid_3527000/3527225.stm |title=How to find space with Becks |date=2 March 2004 |work=BBC Sport |access-date=2 April 2020 |archive-date=14 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210414121205/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sportacademy/hi/sa/football/video_masterclasses/newsid_3527000/3527225.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> as well as his anticipation, composure, determination, athleticism, dedication, and intelligence as a footballer.<ref name="ESPN 2002 Profile"/><ref name="top 20">{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/2374617/The-Top-20.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220110/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/2374617/The-Top-20.html |archive-date=10 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |title=The Top 20 |work=The Telegraph |date=10 March 2004 |access-date=17 April 2020 }}{{cbignore}}</ref>

===Approach to training and praise from managers===
{{Quote box
| width = 28%
| align = right
| quote = "David Beckham is Britain's finest striker of a football not because of God-given talent but because he practises with a relentless application that the vast majority of less gifted players wouldn't contemplate."
| source = —Former Manchester United manager [[Alex Ferguson]].<ref name="guardian.co.uk"/>
}}
Beckham was a product of Sir [[Alex Ferguson]]'s hard-working approach at Manchester United. Ferguson said that Beckham "practised with a discipline to achieve an accuracy that other players wouldn't care about".<ref name="Kings of the free-kick">{{cite news |url=http://www.fifa.com/newscentre/features/news/newsid=1551015/index.html |title=Kings of the free-kick |publisher=FIFA |access-date=20 December 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120617103741/http://www.fifa.com/newscentre/features/news/newsid=1551015/index.html |archive-date=17 June 2012 }}</ref><ref name="Beckham takes a great leap forward">{{cite news|last1=Barclay|first1=Patrick|title=Ferguson happy as Beckham takes a great leap forward|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/manchester-united/2995526/Ferguson-happy-as-Beckham-takes-a-great-leap-forward.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220110/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/teams/manchester-united/2995526/Ferguson-happy-as-Beckham-takes-a-great-leap-forward.html |archive-date=10 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live|newspaper=The Telegraph|access-date=18 December 2014|date=30 December 2000}}{{cbignore}}</ref> Beckham reportedly spent hours practising his free kicks after training sessions had ended.<ref name="United Legends">{{cite web|url=http://www.manutdzone.com/legends/DavidBeckham.htm|title=Manchester United Legends – David Beckham|publisher=manutdzone.com|access-date=28 May 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080818030242/http://www.manutdzone.com/legends/DavidBeckham.htm|archive-date=18 August 2008|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="guardian.co.uk">{{cite web |last=Campbell |first=Paul |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2013/may/17/david-beckham-alex-ferguson-manchester-united |title=David Beckham: product of Sir Alex Ferguson's school of hard graft |work=The Guardian |date=17 May 2013 |access-date=3 October 2013 |archive-date=5 October 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131005160752/http://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2013/may/17/david-beckham-alex-ferguson-manchester-united |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name="Zidane still the master">{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/2400339/Zidane-still-the-master.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220110/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/2400339/Zidane-still-the-master.html |archive-date=10 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |title=Zidane still the master |work=The Telegraph |last1=Hayward |first1=Paul |date=26 April 2003 |access-date=25 October 2019 }}{{cbignore}}</ref>

Beckham maintained his training routine at Real Madrid and even when his relationship with management was strained in early 2007, Real Madrid president [[Ramón Calderón]] and manager [[Fabio Capello]] praised Beckham for maintaining his professionalism and commitment to the club.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iht.com/articles/ap/2007/01/13/sports/EU-SPT-SOC-Real-Madrid-Beckham.php |title=Coach says Beckham won't play again for Real Madrid |work=International Herald Time |date=13 January 2007 |access-date=28 May 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070620123856/http://www.iht.com/articles/ap/2007/01/13/sports/EU-SPT-SOC-Real-Madrid-Beckham.php |archive-date=20 June 2007 }}</ref> Beckham's Real Madrid teammate [[Roberto Carlos]] regarded Beckham to be the best free-kick exponent he had ever seen.<ref name="Roberto Carlos"/> One of the other best free kick exponents of their generation, Roberto Carlos, commented on the dilemma the team faced when they won a free kick on the edge of the penalty area: "I would stand on one side and Beckham on the other but I wanted to see Beckham take the free-kick because it's beautiful how he hits the ball."<ref name="Roberto Carlos">{{cite news|title=Beckham is best says Roberto Carlos|url=https://www.uefa.com/news/01d5-0e70b1cdb2aa-fdc08ead8e7c-1000--beckham-is-best-says-roberto-carlos/|website=[[UEFA]]|date=9 January 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220311073517/https://www.uefa.com/news/01d5-0e70b1cdb2aa-fdc08ead8e7c-1000--beckham-is-best-says-roberto-carlos/|url-status=live |archive-date=11 March 2022|access-date=17 September 2022}}</ref> During Beckham's time with Milan, his manager [[Carlo Ancelotti]] praised the Englishman for his intelligence and work-rate, in particular the improvements he demonstrated to the technical and tactical aspects of his game, which allowed him to compensate for his loss of pace.<ref name="Milan never intended to play David Beckham"/>

His former England manager [[Steve McClaren]] stated: <blockquote>I've been very fortunate to work with some great players and he [Beckham] was one of them. He was a great player, he made the very most of his talents and that was through sheer hard work, professionalism, always doing extra on the training field. He inspired his team-mates through his performances, he was a winner. He was a leader, people followed him.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/may/16/david-beckham-retires-reaction |title=David Beckham retires: 'He was a leader, people followed him' |work=The Guardian |last1=Jackson |first1=Jamie |date=16 May 2013 |access-date=2 April 2020 |archive-date=11 March 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200311200150/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/may/16/david-beckham-retires-reaction |url-status=live }}</ref></blockquote> Arsenal manager [[Arsène Wenger]] stated, "What remains in your memory is his genuine commitment and dedication, his natural humility which he always had, that will stay forever."<ref name="Quote"/>

In May 2013, asked about how he wanted to be remembered in his retirement, Beckham said, "I just want people to see me as a hardworking footballer, someone that's passionate about the game, someone that – every time I stepped on the pitch – I've given everything that I have, because that's how I feel. That's how I look back on it and hope people will see me."<ref name="guardian.co.uk"/>

===Discipline===
Earlier in his career, Beckham's discipline during matches was brought into question on occasion in the media, due to his temper and his tendency to commit rash challenges and pick up unnecessary bookings.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/talking_point/594307.stm |title=Beckham: Help or hindrance? |work=BBC Sport |date=11 January 2000 |access-date=2 April 2020 |archive-date=28 January 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200128011318/http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/talking_point/594307.stm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-fa-summons-beckham-over-poor-discipline-1122910.html |title=Football: FA summons Beckham over poor discipline |newspaper=The Independent |last1=Harris |first1=Nick |date=28 September 1999 |access-date=2 April 2020 |archive-date=18 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230418125015/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football-fa-summons-beckham-over-poor-discipline-1122910.html |url-status=live }}</ref> Beckham was the first England player ever to collect two red cards, and the first England captain to be sent off.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/sport/football/article576493.ece|title=Beckham red card but joy for Sven|newspaper=[[The Times]]|access-date=12 September 2014|archive-date=10 May 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110510204225/http://www.timesonline.co.uk/tol/sport/football/article576493.ece|url-status=dead}}</ref> Beckham's most notorious red card was during the [[1998 FIFA World Cup|1998 World Cup]] after Argentina's [[Diego Simeone]] had fouled him: Beckham, lying face down on the pitch, kicked out at the Argentine midfielder, who fell dramatically.<ref name="Argentina"/> Along with [[Wayne Rooney]], he holds the record for the most red cards for England at international level.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/league-name/story/2057966/headline |title=Wayne Rooney's controversial foul vs. West Ham not his first gaffe |publisher=ESPN FC |date=27 September 2014 |access-date=2 April 2020 |archive-date=11 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200611020744/https://www.espn.com/soccer/league-name/story/2057966/headline |url-status=live }}</ref> His second red card for England came on 8 October 2005, in a [[2006 FIFA World Cup qualification (UEFA)|2006 World Cup qualifier]] against Austria in Manchester.<ref name="Beckham's career red cards"/>

His only red card with Manchester United came on 6 January 2000, in the [[2000 FIFA Club World Championship]] against Necaxa.<ref name="Beckham's career red cards"/> During his time at Real Madrid, he amassed 41 yellow cards and four red cards in La Liga; he also received a red card in a Copa del Rey match against Valencia on 21 January 2004, in Madrid.<ref name="Beckham's career red cards">{{cite news |url=https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-spain-beckham-statbox/statbox-david-beckhams-career-red-cards-idUKL1719114020070217 |title=STATBOX-David Beckham's career red cards |work=Reuters |date=17 February 2007 |access-date=2 April 2020 |archive-date=11 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200611024349/https://uk.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-spain-beckham-statbox/statbox-david-beckhams-career-red-cards-idUKL1719114020070217 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="espnfc.com">{{cite web|url=http://espnfc.com/player/_/id/8880/david-beckham?cc=5739|title=ESPN player statistics: David Beckham|publisher=ESPN FC|access-date=29 April 2013|archive-date=2 June 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130602144129/http://espnfc.com/player/_/id/8880/david-beckham?cc=5739|url-status=live}}</ref> His only red card with LA Galaxy came on 15 August 2009, in a 2–0 home defeat to the Seattle Sounders in MLS.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2009/aug/16/david-beckham-red-card-la-galaxy |title=David Beckham hits new low at LA Galaxy with red card in 17th minute |work=[[The Guardian]] |date=16 August 2009 |access-date=2 April 2020 |archive-date=10 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200610064745/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2009/aug/16/david-beckham-red-card-la-galaxy |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2013/04/29/david-beckhams-only-mls-red-card-la-galaxy-vs-seattle-sounders-2009 |title=David Beckham's only MLS Red Card – LA Galaxy vs Seattle Sounders 2009 |publisher=MLS Soccer |date=29 April 2013 |access-date=2 April 2020 |archive-date=30 July 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200730122934/https://www.mlssoccer.com/post/2013/04/29/david-beckhams-only-mls-red-card-la-galaxy-vs-seattle-sounders-2009 |url-status=live }}</ref> He received one red card while at Paris Saint-Germain, in a match against Evian on 28 April 2013.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/22334844 |title=David Beckham sent off after six minutes in PSG victory |work=BBC Sport |date=29 April 2013 |access-date=3 October 2013 |archive-date=16 October 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131016225936/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/22334844 |url-status=live }}</ref> Between 2000 and 2013, Beckham played 572 competitive games for England, Milan, LA Galaxy, Manchester United, Real Madrid and PSG, and he received nine red cards – one every 63–64 matches, on average.<ref name="espnfc.com"/>

===Reception===
[[File:David Beckham at Madame Tussauds London.jpg|thumb|upright|Wax statue of Beckham at [[Madame Tussauds]], London]]

Despite his success, popularity, and playing ability, critical reception of Beckham was often divided among sporting figures and fans throughout his career, in part – as Subhankar Mondal of ''[[Goal (website)|Goal]]'' notes – due to his ventures off the pitch, and the widespread coverage that his personal life received.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.goal.com/en-india/news/105/main/2008/08/10/812272/debate-is-david-beckham-truly-great |title=Debate: Is David Beckham Truly Great? |publisher=Goal.com |last1=Mondal |first1=Subhankar |date=10 August 2008 |access-date=2 April 2020 |archive-date=11 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200611045426/https://www.goal.com/en-india/news/105/main/2008/08/10/812272/debate-is-david-beckham-truly-great |url-status=live }}</ref> His former Manchester United manager, Alex Ferguson, speculated in 2007 that Beckham's increasing celebrity status, in particular following his highly publicised relationship with his future wife [[Victoria Beckham|Victoria]], had actually had a negative impact on his playing career.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/babb/11573971/David-Beckham-in-40-quotes.html |title=David Beckham in 40 quotes |work=The Telegraph |last1=Richman |first1=Darren |date=2 May 2015 |access-date=2 April 2020 |archive-date=10 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200610151832/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/babb/11573971/David-Beckham-in-40-quotes.html |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2015, he claimed he had only coached four world class players throughout his time at United, excluding Beckham from the list, commenting: "I don't mean to demean or criticise any of the great or very good footballers who played for me during my 26-year career at United, but there were only four who were world class: [[Eric Cantona|Cantona]], [[Ryan Giggs|Giggs]], [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] and [[Paul Scholes|Scholes]]."<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/sir-alex-ferguson-claims-he-managed-just-four-world-class-players-in-26-years-at-manchester-united-10511947.html |title=Sir Alex Ferguson claims he managed just four world class players in 26 years at Manchester United |work=The Independent |last1=Rice |first1=Simon |date=22 September 2015 |access-date=13 April 2020 |archive-date=2 January 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180102124631/http://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/sir-alex-ferguson-claims-he-managed-just-four-world-class-players-in-26-years-at-manchester-united-10511947.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

Upon his departure to LA Galaxy, {{Lang|es|[[El País]]}} reflected on the dichotomy of Beckham's playing career and his status off the pitch, describing him as "the great paradox of world football", also adding: <blockquote>He is the greatest icon on the planet and the cause of such delirium in the media and on the streets, the greatest catwalk model there is. And yet he has been an anti-diva. He was the most galactic of the galacticos off the pitch, but the greatest of earthlings when he walked on to the field.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/european/2315481/Spain-bids-farewell-to-Beckham.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220110/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/european/2315481/Spain-bids-farewell-to-Beckham.html |archive-date=10 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |title=Spain bids farewell to Beckham |work=The Telegraph |last1=Lowe |first1=Sid |date=19 June 2007 |access-date=2 April 2020 }}{{cbignore}}</ref></blockquote> Regarding Beckham's crossing ability, Rob Smyth of ''[[The Guardian]]'' said in 2014: "he was a great crosser and perhaps the greatest of all time", also noting that "he was a dead-ball specialist and also a dying-ball specialist: [...] his signature crosses in open play involved a ball that was barely moving, which allowed him to use the same technique as with corners and free-kicks."<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2014/feb/14/joy-of-six-crosses-david-beckham |title=The Joy of Six: football crosses |work=The Guardian |last1=Smyth |first1=Rob |date=14 February 2014 |access-date=3 April 2020 |archive-date=26 April 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200426113720/https://www.theguardian.com/football/blog/2014/feb/14/joy-of-six-crosses-david-beckham |url-status=live }}</ref> Nigel Reed of [[CBC Sports]] commented on Beckham's career and celebrity status, stating: "His brand is global, his appeal universal. He sparked debate and polarised opinion. But underneath the gloss he was, first and foremost, a very good footballer." He also added that while he felt that "Beckham was not the greatest player of his generation", he believed he had the ability to change games, describing him as "master of his art and a deadly opponent", whose "talent was only topped by his passion".<ref name="Soccer and Spice">{{cite news |url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports-content/soccer/opinion/2013/05/david-beckham-soccer-and-spice.html |title=David Beckham: Soccer and Spice |work=CBC Sports |last1=Reed |first1=Nigel |date=17 May 2013 |access-date=2 April 2020 |archive-date=16 June 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200616210250/https://www.cbc.ca/sports-content/soccer/opinion/2013/05/david-beckham-soccer-and-spice.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Football-related business activities==
===David Beckham Academy===
[[File:David Beckham Academy London at night.jpg|thumb|Beckham Academy in London]]

In 2005, Beckham founded the [[David Beckham Academy]] football school, operating in London and Los Angeles. It was announced in late 2009 that both would close.<ref>{{Cite news |title=California Branch of David Beckham Academy Closes |url=http://www.goal.com/en-us/news/66/united-states/2010/02/08/1781126/california-branch-of-david-beckham-academy-closes |publisher=Goal |access-date=28 November 2010 |date=28 November 2010 |archive-date=15 May 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110515045727/http://www.goal.com/en-us/news/66/united-states/2010/02/08/1781126/california-branch-of-david-beckham-academy-closes |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Inter Miami===
{{Main|Inter Miami CF}}
On 5 February 2014, MLS announced that Beckham had exercised his option to buy a [[Expansion of Major League Soccer|MLS expansion team]] for {{US$|25M}}, which he had received as part of the contract he signed with the LA Galaxy in 2007.<ref name="Kennedy" /> The ownership group, led by Beckham, originally hoped the [[Miami]]-based team would begin play in 2016 or 2017.<ref name="Miami Beckham" /> After delays getting a [[Miami MLS stadium|stadium]] deal completed, MLS announced in January 2018 that the team had been approved, and would likely begin play in 2020.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/42864461|title=David Beckham launches Miami Major League Soccer team|work=BBC Sport|date=29 January 2018|access-date=12 February 2018|archive-date=5 May 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200505114620/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/42864461|url-status=live}}</ref> The team name and crest were revealed on 5 September. Club Internacional de Futbol Miami – more commonly known as Inter Miami – is represented by a black crest with neon pink trimmings and herons whose legs clasp to form an "M" for Miami.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/soccer/fl-sp-miami-soccer-team-crest-20180905-story.html|title=Inter Miami: David Beckham's MLS team unveils name and crest|last1=Lerner|first1=Keven|first2=Doug|last2=Phillips|work=Sun-Sentinel|access-date=5 September 2018|url-status=live|archive-date=12 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181012130359/http://www.sun-sentinel.com/sports/soccer/fl-sp-miami-soccer-team-crest-20180905-story.html}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Inter Miami: David Beckham's MLS team is called Club Internacional de Futbol Miami |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45419289 |access-date=5 September 2018 |work=BBC Sport |archive-date=6 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180906040231/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/45419289 |url-status=live }}</ref> The club made its MLS debut on 1 March 2020 with a 1–0 away loss to [[Los Angeles FC|Los Angeles]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report?gameId=560541|title=LAFC vs. Inter Miami CF – Football Match Report – 1 March 2020 |website=ESPN.com|access-date=2 March 2020|archive-date=2 March 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200302040744/https://www.espn.com/soccer/report?gameId=560541|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Salford City===
In January 2019, it was announced that Beckham was set to join his Class of '92 teammates as part owner of English non-league club [[Salford City F.C.|Salford City]], taking 10% of the club previously held by [[Peter Lim]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46972871|title=David Beckham to become shareholder of National League club Salford|date=23 January 2019|work=BBC Sport|access-date=23 January 2019|archive-date=1 March 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210301081420/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/46972871|url-status=live}}</ref> with the deal being subject to [[Football Association]] approval. On 31 January, the club announced that the FA had approved him to become a director of the club.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47077888|title=David Beckham: Salford City directorship approved by Football Association|date=31 January 2019|work=BBC Sport|access-date=1 February 2019|archive-date=22 October 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201022160001/https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47077888|url-status=live}}</ref> In May 2025, Beckham and Gary Neville led a new consortium taking over Salford.<ref>{{cite news|access-date=May 8, 2026|last= Ornstein|first=David=2026-05-08|title= David Beckham and Gary Neville lead new consortium taking over Salford|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6340647/2025/05/08/david-beckham-gary-neville-salford/|work= The New York Times|language=en-US}}</ref>

==Personal life==
[[File:David Beckham Victoria Beckham 2019.jpg|thumb|Beckham and wife [[Victoria Beckham|Victoria]] in 2019]]

In 1997, Beckham started dating [[Victoria Beckham|Victoria Adams]] after she attended a Manchester United match.<ref name="mend">{{Cite news |url=http://news.independent.co.uk/people/profiles/article55497.ece |title=David and Victoria Beckham: Can they mend it like Beckhams? |work=The Independent |date=11 April 2005 |access-date=3 September 2018|location=London |first=Alison |last=Roberts |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071228201145/http://news.independent.co.uk/people/profiles/article55497.ece |archive-date=28 December 2007 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.lamondamagazine.com/en/m/defense/victoria-beckham/ |title=Victoria Beckham owes me everything |first=Juliette |last=Wills |date=21 July 2013 |website=La Monda |access-date=3 September 2018 |archive-date=3 September 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180903151008/http://www.lamondamagazine.com/en/m/defense/victoria-beckham/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name=idolsw>{{cite web |url=http://www.wmagazine.com/celebrities/2007/08/beckhams_steven_klein?currentPage=2 |title=American Idols |work=[[W (magazine)|W]] |date=1 January 2010 |access-date=3 September 2018|url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090214155704/http://www.wmagazine.com/celebrities/2007/08/beckhams_steven_klein?currentPage=2 |archive-date=14 February 2009 }}</ref> She was famously known as "Posh Spice" of the pop music group [[Spice Girls]], one of Britain's top pop groups at the time, and his team was also enjoying a great run of success. Their relationship instantly attracted a great deal of media attention. The couple were dubbed "[[Posh and Becks]]" by the media.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/entertainment/6295214.stm |title=Will Brand Beckham break America? |last=Pryor |first=Fiona |date=12 July 2007 |work=[[BBC News]] |access-date=3 September 2018 |archive-date=11 March 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090311093221/http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/entertainment/6295214.stm |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 4 July 1999, they were married by the [[Bishop of Cork, Cloyne and Ross|Bishop of Cork]], [[Paul Colton]], at [[Luttrellstown Castle]] in Ireland.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/special_report/1999/07/99/the_posh_wedding/385866.stm |title=Wedded spice |date=5 July 1999 |work=[[BBC News]] |access-date=26 November 2011 |archive-date=7 September 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170907003627/http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/special_report/1999/07/99/the_posh_wedding/385866.stm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Bishop who tied celebrity knot is a United fan |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/news/bishop-who-tied-celebrity-knot-is-a-united-fan-1.203362 |website=www.irishtimes.com |quote=The two stars are originally Church of England members but had no difficulty with a wedding in the sister church on this side of the Irish Sea. And Bishop Colton was only too pleased to officiat |access-date=20 June 2025 |archive-date=8 December 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241208212519/https://www.irishtimes.com/news/bishop-who-tied-celebrity-knot-is-a-united-fan-1.203362 |url-status=live }}</ref> Beckham's teammate [[Gary Neville]] was the best man,<ref name="mend"/> and the couple's four-month-old son, Brooklyn, was the ring bearer.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/special_report/1999/07/99/the_posh_wedding/383151.stm |title=David and Victoria tie the knot |work=BBC News |date=5 July 1999 |access-date=3 September 2018 |archive-date=3 March 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080303110445/http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/special_report/1999/07/99/the_posh_wedding/383151.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> The media were kept away from the ceremony, as the Beckhams had an exclusive deal with ''[[OK!|OK! Magazine]]'', but newspapers were able to obtain photographs of them sitting on golden thrones.<ref>{{cite news |title=Sun pips OK! to Posh wedding photos |work=BBC News |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/special_report/1999/07/99/the_posh_wedding/387126.stm |access-date=25 May 2006 |date=6 July 1999 |archive-date=6 July 2006 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060706182022/http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/special_report/1999/07/99/the_posh_wedding/387126.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> 437 staff were employed for the wedding reception, which was estimated to have cost {{GBP|500,000}}.<ref>{{cite news |title=Wedded spice |work=BBC News |date=5 July 1999 |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/special_report/1999/07/99/the_posh_wedding/385866.stm |access-date=2 December 2005 |archive-date=7 September 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170907003627/http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/special_report/1999/07/99/the_posh_wedding/385866.stm |url-status=live }}</ref>

Beckham has [[obsessive–compulsive disorder]] (OCD), which he says makes him "have everything in a straight line or everything has to be in pairs." Victoria claimed: "If you open our fridge, it's all co-ordinated down either side. We've got three fridges – food in one, salad in another and drinks in the third. In the drinks one, everything is symmetrical. If there's three cans, he'll throw one away because it has to be an even number."<ref name="OCD">{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/this-britain/beckham-reveals-his-battle-with-obsessive-disorder-472573.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080605122351/http://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/this-britain/beckham-reveals-his-battle-with-obsessive-disorder-472573.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=5 June 2008 |title=Beckham reveals his battle with obsessive disorder |access-date=28 August 2012 |location=London |work=The Independent |first=Maxine |last=Frith |date=3 April 2006}}</ref> A staunch [[Monarchism|monarchist]], Beckham [[Queue for the lying-in-state of Elizabeth II|queued for 12 hours]] in September 2022 to see [[Death and state funeral of Elizabeth II#Lying-in-state|Queen Elizabeth II lying in state]] at [[Westminster Hall]].<ref>{{Cite news |title=David Beckham on his wait to see the Queen lying in state |work=BBC News |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/av/uk-62927306 |access-date=16 September 2022 |archive-date=16 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220916141030/https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/av/uk-62927306 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Sansome |first=Jessica |date=16 September 2022 |title=David Beckham dons flat cap and suit as he queues for Queen lying in state |url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/showbiz-news/david-beckham-dons-flat-cap-25037458 |access-date=16 September 2022 |website=Manchester Evening News |archive-date=16 September 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220916142251/https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/showbiz-news/david-beckham-dons-flat-cap-25037458 |url-status=live }}</ref>

<!--[[Sarah Marbeck redirect points to this section]]-->
In 2004, various newspapers carried claims by Beckham's former personal assistant [[Rebecca Loos]] that she and Beckham had engaged in an extramarital affair.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/3614993.stm |title=Beckham story is tabloids' dream |work=BBC News |date=9 April 2004 |access-date=4 May 2009 |archive-date=22 April 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090422151445/http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/uk/3614993.stm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.timesonline.co.uk/article/0,,1-1066358,00.html |title=Beckham flies back to Madrid from holiday |work=[[The Times]] |location=London |date=7 April 2004 |access-date=4 May 2009 |archive-date=8 November 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231108152955/https://www.thetimes.co.uk/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> A week later, the Malaysian-born Australian model Sarah Marbeck claimed that she had slept with Beckham on two occasions. Beckham dismissed both claims as "ludicrous".<ref>{{cite news |title=Beckham to stay in Spain |work=BBC Sport |date=20 May 2004 |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/sport2/hi/football/europe/3733607.stm |access-date=7 October 2005 |archive-date=25 March 2006 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060325202240/http://news.bbc.co.uk/sport1/hi/football/europe/3733607.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> A documentary called ''[[Beckham (TV series)|Beckham]]'' was released in 2023 on Netflix, 20 years after the alleged affair with Rebecca Loos took place. In it, Beckham did not deny the affair took place; instead, he stated how hard that general period was on his marriage.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2023/oct/27/digested-week-rebecca-loos-can-hold-her-peace-no-longer | title=Digested week: Rebecca Loos can hold her peace no longer | newspaper=The Guardian | date=27 October 2023 | last1=Brockes | first1=Emma }}</ref>

Beckham has been actively involved in [[beekeeping]], [[animal husbandry]] and [[Agriculture|farming]] since 2020 in the [[barn]] they bought in the [[Cotswolds]] in 2016.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.hellomagazine.com/celebrities/552940/david-beckham-incredible-garden-cotswolds-home-veg-patch/|title=David Beckham's incredible garden at {{GBP|12M}} Cotswolds home is a feast for the eyes|date=14 May 2024|website=HELLO!|access-date=27 December 2024|archive-date=14 May 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240514163926/https://www.hellomagazine.com/celebrities/552940/david-beckham-incredible-garden-cotswolds-home-veg-patch/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://people.com/victoria-beckham-jokes-give-me-my-husband-back-as-david-farms-8708204|title=Victoria Beckham Jokes 'Give Me My Husband Back' as David Goes into Farmer Mode with Chickens and Vegetables|website=People|access-date=27 December 2024|archive-date=27 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241227133355/https://people.com/victoria-beckham-jokes-give-me-my-husband-back-as-david-farms-8708204|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.farmersguardian.com/news/4116733/david-beckham-poses-farming-stars-visit-jeremy-clarksons-diddly-squat-farm|title=David Beckham poses with farming stars on visit to Jeremy Clarkson's Diddly Squat Farm|date=30 May 2023|work=Farmers Guardian|access-date=27 December 2024|archive-date=27 December 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20241227135802/https://www.farmersguardian.com/news/4116733/david-beckham-poses-farming-stars-visit-jeremy-clarksons-diddly-squat-farm|url-status=live}}</ref>
Since 2022, following Brooklyn Beckham's [[marriage]] to [[Actor|actress]] [[Nicola Peltz]], reports of tension between David Beckham and his eldest son have appeared in the press. Some media outlets have described differences in lifestyle and family dynamics, as well as speculation about strained relations within the Beckham family.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Why has Brooklyn Beckham fallen out with his parents? |url=https://www.heart.co.uk/showbiz/why-has-brooklyn-beckham-fallen-out-with-parents-victoria-david/ |access-date=2026-03-31 |website=Heart |language=en}}</ref>

Beckham was [[Knight|knighted]] by [[Charles III|King Charles III]] at [[Windsor Castle]] in November 2025, in recognition of his services to sport and charitable causes.<ref>{{cite news |date=4 November 2025 |title=David Beckham knighted as King Charles honours former Manchester United and England star at Windsor Castle |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/13463742/david-beckham-knighted-as-king-charles-honours-former-manchester-united-and-england-star-at-windsor-castle |access-date=4 November 2025 |work=Sky Sports}}</ref> He received a star on the [[Hollywood Walk of Fame]] in June 2026, attended by his wife Victoria and three of their children in Los Angeles.<ref>{{cite web |last=Sacks |first=Hannah |url=https://people.com/david-beckham-poses-with-3-of-his-4-kids-at-hollywood-walk-of-fame-ceremony-11996797 |title=David Beckham Poses with Wife Victoria and 3 of His 4 Kids at Hollywood Walk of Fame Ceremony |publisher=People |date=12 June 2026 }}</ref>

===Legal issues===
In September 2010, Beckham announced that he was making a court application against prostitute Irma Nici and several others over claims in the magazine ''[[In Touch Weekly|In Touch]]'' that he had had sex with her.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.dailytelegraph.com.au/entertainment/david-beckhams-lawyers-serve-25-million-writ-on-prostitute-irma-nici/story-e6frewyr-1225929589722 |title=David Beckham's lawyers serve US$25 million writ on prostitute Irma Nici |work=The Daily Telegraph |date=27 September 2010 |access-date=10 June 2012 |archive-date=26 September 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120926032240/http://www.dailytelegraph.com.au/entertainment/david-beckhams-lawyers-serve-25-million-writ-on-prostitute-irma-nici/story-e6frewyr-1225929589722 |url-status=live }}</ref> His court application was dismissed under US freedom of speech laws, and the magazine later accepted that the allegations against Beckham were untrue.<ref>{{cite news|title=David Beckham loses In Touch, Irma Nici lawsuit: Judge says cheating story is of public interest|work=[[Daily News (New York)|Daily News]]|location=New York|url=http://www.nydailynews.com/entertainment/gossip/david-beckham-loses-touch-irma-nici-lawsuit-judge-cheating-story-public-interest-article-1.133622|date=14 February 2011|access-date=11 January 2016|archive-date=22 February 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160222140659/http://www.nydailynews.com/entertainment/gossip/david-beckham-loses-touch-irma-nici-lawsuit-judge-cheating-story-public-interest-article-1.133622|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=David Beckham loses appeal to sue magazine over prostitute Irma Nici's false claims|url=http://www.news.com.au/entertainment/celebrity-life/david-beckham-loses-appeal-to-sue-magazine-over-prostitute-irma-nicis-false-claims/story-e6frfmqi-1226599012614|date=17 March 2013|work=news.com.au|access-date=11 January 2016|archive-date=7 February 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160207200855/http://www.news.com.au/entertainment/celebrity-life/david-beckham-loses-appeal-to-sue-magazine-over-prostitute-irma-nicis-false-claims/story-e6frfmqi-1226599012614|url-status=dead}}</ref>

On 9 May 2019, at Bromley Magistrates Court, Beckham was banned from driving for six months. He previously pleaded guilty to using a mobile phone while driving on 21 November 2018. The court heard he was photographed by a member of the public holding a phone as he drove in "slowly moving" traffic. Beckham received six points on his licence, to add to the six he already had for previous speeding matters. He was also fined {{GBP|750}}, and ordered to pay {{GBP|100}} in prosecution costs and a {{GBP|75}} surcharge fee.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-london-48213106 |title=Beckham banned for using phone in Bentley |work=BBC News |date=9 May 2019 |access-date=9 May 2019 |archive-date=9 May 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190509154837/https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-london-48213106 |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Tattoos===
{{as of|2021}}, Beckham has more than 65 [[tattoo]]s covering a large part of his body, including tattoos on his hands, neck and head.<ref>{{cite web |title=A Guide to David Beckham's 60 Plus Tattoos |url=https://www.menshealth.com/entertainment/a36339426/david-beckham-tattoos/ |work=menshealth.com |date=6 May 2021 |access-date=30 May 2021 |archive-date=2 June 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210602214641/https://www.menshealth.com/entertainment/a36339426/david-beckham-tattoos/ |url-status=live }}</ref> There are names of his sons Romeo, Cruz and Brooklyn, and of his wife Victoria. His wife's name, tattooed on his left forearm, is in the [[Devanagari]] script (used for the Hindi and Sanskrit languages, among others) because Beckham thought it would be "tacky" to have it in English. However, this was misspelt as the equivalent of "Vhictoria".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/entertainment/1044797.stm |title=Beckham's tattoo misspelt |work=BBC News |date=28 November 2000 |access-date=27 October 2013 |archive-date=15 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170815033644/http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/entertainment/1044797.stm |url-status=live }}</ref> In his autobiography ''David Beckham: My Side'', he said that the idea of having tattoos came to him in 1999 after his son Brooklyn was born, following a conversation on the subject of tattoos with [[Mel B]] (then Mel G) and her then-husband, Jimmy Gulzar. Beckham said: "When you see me, you see the tattoos. You see an expression of how I feel about Victoria and the boys. They're part of me."<ref>Beckham, David (2010). "David Beckham: My Side". HarperCollins</ref>

He has several tattoos that pay tribute to his daughter, Harper, as well as several with religious significance.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/3am/celebrity-news/david-beckhams-tattoos-explained-every-12761443|title=Every David Beckham tattoo explained – from Victoria's to the mistake|last=Jenkins|first=John|date=22 June 2018|website=Daily Mirror|access-date=30 March 2020|archive-date=11 June 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200611000529/https://www.mirror.co.uk/3am/celebrity-news/david-beckhams-tattoos-explained-every-12761443|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2018, Beckham added to his collection a tattoo of a solar system covering the left side of his scalp.<ref>{{cite news |last=Haynes |first=Gavin |title=Hooked on ink: is it possible to be 'addicted' to tattoos? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/fashion/shortcuts/2018/may/01/addicted-to-tattoos-david-beckham-body-art |access-date=19 October 2018 |work=The Guardian |date=1 May 2018 |archive-date=19 October 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181019121926/https://www.theguardian.com/fashion/shortcuts/2018/may/01/addicted-to-tattoos-david-beckham-body-art |url-status=live }}</ref> Many of Beckham's tattoos were completed by the Manchester-based tattoo artist [[Louis Molloy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.insider.com/david-beckham-tattoo-artist-says-he-feels-no-pain-2018-10|title=David Beckham 'feels absolutely no pain,' according to his tattoo artist|last=Murray|first=Tom|website=Insider|access-date=30 March 2020}}</ref>

===Leaked emails===

In 2015, a Portuguese company associated with Beckham's spokesman had their server hacked which contained personal emails from Beckham. Germany's ''Der Spiegel'' and France's ''L'Equipe'' published details of the hack, reporting how Beckham was angry at not being granted a knighthood in 2013, and that the [[Honours Committee]] was concerned about his tax affairs due to input from UK government department [[HM Revenue and Customs|HMRC]]. Beckham's team stated some of the published emails were doctored, but they confirmed others as genuine.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2017/feb/06/hacked-david-beckham-emails-renders-injunction-worthless | title=Publication of hacked David Beckham emails renders injunction worthless | newspaper=The Guardian | date=6 February 2017 | last1=Booth | first1=Robert | last2=Grierson | first2=Jamie }}</ref>

==Celebrity status and commercial partnerships==
[[File:David Beckham 2009.jpg|thumb|upright|Beckham in [[Cape Town]], South Africa, in 2009]]

Beckham's relationship and marriage to Victoria, famous in her own right as part of the [[Spice Girls]], contributed to his celebrityhood beyond football. Beckham became known as a fashion icon, and together with Victoria, the couple became lucrative spokespeople sought after by clothing designers, health and fitness specialists, fashion magazines, and perfume and cosmetics manufacturers. Early endorsements included the British hair styling brand [[Brylcreem]] for {{GBP|4M}} in 1997, which saw him appear in UK commercials.<ref name="Acting">{{cite news |title=David Beckham: a history in ads |url=https://www.marketingweek.com/david-beckham-a-history-in-ads/ |access-date=10 July 2021 |magazine=Marketing Week |archive-date=11 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210711120814/https://www.marketingweek.com/david-beckham-a-history-in-ads/ |url-status=live }}</ref> In 2002, he was hailed as the ultimate "[[metrosexual]]" by the man who invented the term<ref>{{cite web |url=http://dir.salon.com/story/ent/feature/2002/07/22/metrosexual/print.html |title=Meet the metrosexual |work=Salon |access-date=13 November 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081113123551/http://dir.salon.com/story/ent/feature/2002/07/22/metrosexual/print.html |archive-date=13 November 2008 }}</ref> and has been described as such by numerous other articles since.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.marksimpson.com/blog/2007/07/13/america-meet-david-beckham/ |title=America – meet David Beckham |publisher=Marksimpson.com |access-date=13 November 2008|date=13 July 2007 }}</ref> The various iconic hairstyles he sported throughout his career –including a [[buzz cut]], a [[Mohawk hairstyle|Mohawk]], and a [[ponytail]]– were widely covered in the media.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/gallery/2013/may/17/david-beckham-hairstyles-pictures |title=David Beckham: a career in hairstyles – in pictures |work=The Guardian |last1=Hogan |first1=Michael |date=17 May 2013 |access-date=4 April 2020 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.gq.com/story/how-to-get-every-david-beckham-haircut |title=How to Get Every David Beckham Haircut |work=GQ |last1=Kilbane |first1=Brennan |date=23 August 2018 |access-date=4 April 2020 }}</ref>

While heterosexual, Beckham actively courted a gay fanbase and openly supported [[gay media]], preferring to give interviews to publications that supported the [[LGBTQ community]]. He came to be called a "[[gay icon]]" – a term he embraces – for his popularity among the gay community.<ref name=":0">{{cite news |last1=Masters |first1=James |date=17 May 2013 |title=Beckham: The man who broke football's gay taboo? |publisher=[[CNN]] |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2013/05/17/sport/football/football-david-beckham-gay-icon-fashion/index.html |access-date=24 May 2021}}</ref> This honorific has been in dispute, however, since Beckham signed a deal with [[Qatar]] (which [[LGBT rights in Qatar|persecutes LGBT people]]) to become a brand ambassador for the [[2022 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=18 November 2022 |title='A gay icon no more': will David Beckham's Qatar role kill his brand? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/nov/18/will-david-beckham-qatar-role-kill-his-brand-world-cup |access-date=19 November 2022 |work=The Guardian }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=18 November 2022 |title='A gay icon no more': will David Beckham's Qatar role kill his brand? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2022/nov/18/will-david-beckham-qatar-role-kill-his-brand-world-cup |access-date=19 November 2022 |website=The Guardian }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |first1=Sammy |last1=Mngqosini |first2=Zayn |last2=Nabbi |date=14 November 2022 |title=David Beckham's 'status as a gay icon will be shredded' if he continues as Qatar World Cup ambassador says British comedian |url=https://www.cnn.com/2022/11/14/football/david-beckham-qatar-world-cup-spt-intl/index.html |access-date=20 November 2022 |website=CNN }}</ref> In a statement, Beckham said that the World Cup will be "[a platform for] progress, inclusivity and tolerance".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Armstrong |first=Jeremy |date=18 November 2022 |title=David Beckham breaks silence on {{GBP|150M}} Qatar ambassador role as criticism grows |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/david-beckham-qatar-world-cup-28525203 |access-date=19 November 2022 |website=The Mirror }}</ref>

The Beckhams were paid {{US$|13.7{{nbsp}}million}} in 2007 to launch his fragrance line in the US.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://uk.eonline.com/news/419662/david-beckham-s-incredible-soccer-career-by-the-numbers|title=David Beckham's career by the numbers|date=16 May 2013|publisher=E!|access-date=12 September 2014}}</ref> In the world of fashion, David has appeared on the covers of many magazines. US covers have included the men's magazine ''[[Details (magazine)|Details]]'', and with Victoria for the August 2007 issue of ''[[W (magazine)|W]]''.<ref>{{cite web|title=The Beckhams: American Idols: W Feature Story on Style.com |url=http://www.style.com/w/feat_story/071107|publisher=Style.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080718213746/http://www.style.com/w/feat_story/071107|archive-date=18 July 2008}}</ref> According to Google, "David Beckham" was searched for more than any other sports topic on their site in 2003 and 2004.<ref>{{cite web |title=2003 Year-End Google Zeitgeist |url=https://www.google.com/press/zeitgeist2003.html |access-date=9 October 2005 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=2004 Year-End Google Zeitgeist |url=https://www.google.com/press/zeitgeist2004.html |access-date=9 October 2005 }}</ref> According to [[Ask Jeeves]], Beckham ranked third among subjects most searched for by British users of that site in the first decade of the 2000s.<ref>{{cite news |title=Britney Spears tops Noughties web search list |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/celebritynews/6858806/Britney-Spears-tops-Noughties-web-search-list.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220110/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/celebritynews/6858806/Britney-Spears-tops-Noughties-web-search-list.html |archive-date=10 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |work=The Telegraph |date=21 December 2009 |access-date=17 May 2014}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

[[File:Michelle Obama with David Beckham 2012.jpg|thumb|left|Beckham with United States First Lady [[Michelle Obama]] at the White House, 15 March 2012]]

Upon their arrival in Los Angeles on 12 July 2007, the night before Beckham's formal introduction, [[Los Angeles International Airport]] was filled with paparazzi and news reporters.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scotsman.com/lifestyle/the-beckhams-go-to-hollywood-1-909020/|title=The Beckhams go to Hollywood|website=The Scotsman}}</ref> On the next night, Victoria appeared on ''[[The Tonight Show]]'' with [[Jay Leno]] to talk about their move to LA and her [[NBC]] TV show ''[[Victoria Beckham: Coming to America]]''.<ref>{{cite web|title=NBC.com – Victoria Beckham Coming To America |url=http://www.nbc.com/Victoria_Beckham/|publisher=NBC.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070714101927/http://www.nbc.com/Victoria_Beckham/|archive-date=14 July 2007}}</ref> On 22 July, a private welcoming party was held for the couple at the [[Museum of Contemporary Art, Los Angeles]]. [[A-list]] celebrities attending included [[Steven Spielberg]], [[Jim Carrey]], [[George Clooney]], [[Tom Cruise]], [[Katie Holmes]], [[Will Smith]], [[Jada Pinkett Smith]], and [[Oprah Winfrey]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Eller |first=Claudia |url=https://www.latimes.com/business/la-fi-beckham19jul19,1,1699340.story |title=Hollywood breathlessly awaits Beckhams |work=Los Angeles Times |date=19 July 2007 |access-date=4 May 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090403003158/http://www.latimes.com/business/la-fi-beckham19jul19%2C1%2C1699340.story?track=rss |archive-date=3 April 2009 }}</ref>

Beckham's many endorsement deals make him one of the most recognizable athletes throughout the world. Having worn [[Adidas]] football boots from the start of his career (notably [[Adidas Predator]]), in 2003 he signed a {{US$|160M}} lifetime contract with Adidas, earning nearly half the money upfront, and would continue to earn percentages of profits on all of his branded Adidas products.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.independent.ie/woman/celeb-news/the-face-of-ten-celebrities-who-have-earned-big-bucks-from-endorsements-29958509.html|title=The face of&nbsp;... Ten celebrities who have earned big bucks from endorsements|work=The Irish Independent|date=28 January 2014 |access-date=12 September 2014}}</ref> His 2004 Adidas television commercial "Kicking it", in which he appears with England Rugby World Cup winner [[Jonny Wilkinson]], was voted among the best British commercials of the year, and featured as one of the Great Ads of the 21st Century in Channel 4's 2004 update of [[The 100 Greatest TV Ads]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Adidas 'Kicking it' ad sails into top 50 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/media/2004/sep/17/newmedia.advertising |access-date=2 November 2022 |newspaper=The Guardian}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=The 100 Greatest TV Ads |url=https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=Kj14p4nulUw |access-date=2 November 2022 |publisher=Channel 4 |date=29 August 2004}}</ref> He had a 10-year collaboration with [[PepsiCo]] that expired in 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/pepsi-looking-for-economies-splits-with-the-expensive-david-beckham/|title=Pepsi, Looking for Economies, Splits With the Expensive David Beckham|date=3 January 2009|work=[[CBS News]]}}</ref> He has also promoted [[The Walt Disney Company]] theme parks.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/david-beckham-endorsing-disney/|title=David Beckham Endorsing Disney|website=[[CBS News]]|date=26 January 2007|access-date=12 September 2014}}</ref> In April 2021, he became a global ambassador for [[Maserati]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Maserati and David Beckham: Global Ambassador &#124; Maserati|url=https://www.maserati.com/international/en/news/maserati-and-david-beckham#:~:text=David%20Beckham%20said:%20%E2%80%9CIt%27s%20an,very%20best%20innovation%20and%20design.&text=The%20movie%20sees%20the%20Maserati,performance%20SUV%20-%20the%20Levante%20Trofeo.|access-date=18 September 2021|website=www.maserati.com|archive-date=6 April 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220406220652/https://www.maserati.com/international/en/news/maserati-and-david-beckham#:~:text=David%20Beckham%20said:%20%E2%80%9CIt%27s%20an,very%20best%20innovation%20and%20design.&text=The%20movie%20sees%20the%20Maserati,performance%20SUV%20-%20the%20Levante%20Trofeo.|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Maserati et David Beckham inaugurent la collection Fuoriserie Essentials |url=https://www.motorlegend.com/actualite-automobile/maserati-et-david-beckham-inaugurent-la-collection-fuoriserie-essentials/25336.html |access-date=23 June 2023 |website=Motor Legend}}</ref> In 2023, as part of Maserati's new personalisation programme, "Fuoriserie Essentials", the brand unveiled its first collection with Beckham.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Maserati dévoile sa première collection automobile avec David Beckham |url=https://www.bfmtv.com/luxe/lifestyle/maserati-devoile-sa-premiere-collection-automobile-avec-david-beckham_GN-202306160408.html |access-date=23 June 2023 |website=BFM TV|date=16 June 2023 }}</ref><ref name=":1" />

Beckham has several eponymous video games, including ''[[Go! Go! Beckham! Adventure on Soccer Island]]'', a [[platform game]] for the [[Game Boy Advance]], and ''[[David Beckham Soccer]]'', a football game for a number of [[Video game platforms#Platforms|platforms]],<ref name="Eurogamer">{{cite web |first=Tom |last=Bramwell |title=Go!Go! Beckham! Adventure on Soccer Island Review |url=http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/r_gogobeckham_gba |website=[[Eurogamer]] |date=12 September 2002 |access-date=8 June 2009 }}</ref><ref name="beckhamxbox">{{cite web|title=David Beckham Soccer Review |last=Varanini |first=Giancarlo |date=14 August 2002 |website=[[GameSpot]] |url=http://www.gamespot.com/xbox/sports/davidbeckhamsoccer/review.html |access-date=8 June 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090828060405/http://www.gamespot.com/xbox/sports/davidbeckhamsoccer/review.html |archive-date=28 August 2009 }}</ref> and he was brand ambassador for exercise video game ''[[EA Sports Active 2]]''.<ref>{{cite news |title=EA lands Beckham for brand ambassador role |url=http://www.marketingmagazine.co.uk/article/1023006/ea-lands-beckham-brand-ambassador-role |first=John |last=Reynolds |work=Marketing |date=18 August 2010 |access-date=17 May 2014}}</ref> Beckham featured in [[EA Sports]]' [[FIFA (video game series)|''FIFA'' video game series]]; he was on the cover for the UK edition of ''[[FIFA: Road to World Cup 98|FIFA 98]]''. During his playing career (which ended in May 2013), Beckham generated an estimated {{GBP|1&nbsp;billion}} in [[Kit (association football)#Basic equipment|shirt]] and [[football boot|boot]] sales.<ref name="honours"/> In 2006, [[Lloyd's of London]] insured his legs for {{GBP|100M}}.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Grant|first1=Katie|last2=Papasian|first2=John|title=Premium cover|work=[[i (British newspaper)|The i]]|issue=1435|date=2 July 2015|page=2|editor-last=Duff|editor-first=Oliver|editor-link=Oliver Duff (British editor)}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.lloyds.com/lloyds/about-us/history/innovation-and-unusual-risks/going-out-on-a-limb|title=GOING OUT ON A LIMB – BODY PARTS AND OTHERS|access-date=3 July 2015|website=Lloyd's.com|archive-date=4 July 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150704193008/https://www.lloyds.com/lloyds/about-us/history/innovation-and-unusual-risks/going-out-on-a-limb|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2026, Beckham was added to [[Fortnite]].

[[File:Vinfast-D.Beckham-Miss Vietnam.jpg|thumb|Beckham with Miss Vietnam [[Trần Tiểu Vy]] at the Paris Motor Show 2018]]

Beckham played a critical part in bringing the Olympics to London in 2012, travelling with the British delegation to [[Singapore]] in 2005 for the host city selection.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/players/david-beckham/10063146/David-Beckham-retires-key-role-in-London-2012-Olympic-bid-is-praised-by-Lord-Coe.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220110/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/players/david-beckham/10063146/David-Beckham-retires-key-role-in-London-2012-Olympic-bid-is-praised-by-Lord-Coe.html |archive-date=10 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live|title=David Beckham retires: key role in London 2012 Olympic bid is praised by Lord Coe|last=Hart|first=Simon|newspaper=The Daily Telegraph|date=16 May 2013|access-date=7 September 2018|issn=0307-1235}}{{cbignore}}</ref> At the [[2008 Beijing Olympics]] closing ceremony, Beckham, [[Jimmy Page]], and [[Leona Lewis]] represented Britain during the handover segment for the 2012 Olympics. Beckham rode a [[AEC Routemaster|London double-decker bus]] into the stadium and Page and Lewis performed "[[Whole Lotta Love]]".<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/olympics/2303411/London-rap-troupe-fly-flag-at-Beijing-Olympics.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220110/https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/olympics/2303411/London-rap-troupe-fly-flag-at-Beijing-Olympics.html |archive-date=10 January 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |title=London rap troupe fly flag at Beijing Olympics |first=Tom |last=Knight |work=[[The Daily Telegraph]] |date=17 June 2008 |location=London |issn=0307-1235 |oclc=49632006 |access-date=5 December 2017}}{{cbignore}}</ref> He featured at the [[2012 Summer Olympics opening ceremony]], carrying the [[Olympic flame]] to the [[London Stadium|stadium]] by speedboat.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/olympics/19016797|title=David Beckham 'proud' of Olympics 2012 role|date=28 July 2012|work=BBC Sport|access-date=7 September 2018}}</ref>

Beckham visited Afghanistan in May 2010 for a morale-boosting visit to British troops fighting the [[Taliban insurgency]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://sports.gaeatimes.com/2010/05/22/beckham-flies-to-afghanistan-to-boost-british-troops-morale-104019/ |title=Beckham flies to Afghanistan to boost British troops' morale |publisher=Sports.gaeatimes.com |date=22 May 2010 |access-date=10 June 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120723071831/http://sports.gaeatimes.com/2010/05/22/beckham-flies-to-afghanistan-to-boost-british-troops-morale-104019/ |archive-date=23 July 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://sports.gaeatimes.com/2010/05/23/beckham-visits-british-troops-in-afghanistan-104343/ |title=Beckham visits British troops in Afghanistan |publisher=Sports.gaeatimes.com |date=23 May 2010 |access-date=10 June 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120723071836/http://sports.gaeatimes.com/2010/05/23/beckham-visits-british-troops-in-afghanistan-104343/ |archive-date=23 July 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The appearance of Beckham as well as British Foreign Secretary [[William Hague]] and Defence Secretary [[Liam Fox]] was believed to have prompted a [[Taliban]] attack on [[Kandahar]] airfield.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://sports.rediff.com/report/2010/may/24/beckham-targetted-by-taliban-in-afghanistan.htm |title=Beckham targetted by Taliban in Afghanistan? |work=Rediff.com |date=24 May 2010 |access-date=10 June 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Anoop |last=Kumar |publisher=MyNews Interactive Media Co. |url=http://www.mynews.in/News/Taliban_targeted_Beckham_in_Afghanistan!_N57377.html |title=Taliban targeted Beckham in Afghanistan! |date=24 May 2010 |access-date=10 June 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120301205044/http://www.mynews.in/News/Taliban_targeted_Beckham_in_Afghanistan%21_N57377.html |archive-date=1 March 2012 }}</ref>

Chinese authorities appointed Beckham as global ambassador for Chinese football in March 2013. After numerous officials had been banned for match-fixing, and the [[Chinese Super League]] had failed to retain the services of well-known international names, Beckham's role was to help improve the image of the game and raise its profile both in China and abroad.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/news-and-comment/david-beckham-named-as-global-ambassador-for-chinese-football-8518912.html |title=David Beckham named as global ambassador for Chinese football |agency=Reuters |newspaper=The Independent |date=4 March 2013 |access-date=17 May 2014}}</ref>

From 14 July 2013, Beckham appeared in adverts for [[BSkyB]], advertising their [[Sky Sports]] coverage via the [[Sky Go]] app.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.digitalspy.co.uk/showbiz/news/a498247/david-beckham-stars-in-sky-sports-tv-advert-video.html |title=David Beckham stars in Sky Sports TV advert – video – Showbiz News |website=Digital Spy |date=14 July 2013 |access-date=3 October 2013}}</ref> In January 2014, Beckham appeared on ''[[Late Night with Jimmy Fallon]]'' on NBC in the US, and in March he made a guest appearance in the BBC's [[Sport Relief 2014 Special|Sport Relief special]] of ''[[Only Fools and Horses]]''.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/tv/news/sport-relief-2014-david-beckham-makes-acting-debut-only-fools-and-horses-debut-beckham-in-peckham-9208768.html|title=Sport Relief 2014: Watch David Beckham in Peckham in Only Fools and Horses special|work=The Independent|access-date=12 September 2014}}</ref> He was named one of ''[[GQ]]''{{'}}s 50 best dressed British men in 2015.<ref name="gq-magazine.co.uk"/>

In March 2015, Beckham had the third highest social media rank in the world among sportspeople, behind [[Cristiano Ronaldo]] and [[Lionel Messi]], with more than 52 million Facebook fans.<ref>{{cite news|title=Cristiano Ronaldo overtakes Shakira as Facebook's most 'liked' person|url=https://uk.news.yahoo.com/cristiano-ronaldo-overtakes-shakira-as-facebook-s-most--liked-person-085815659-soccer.html|publisher=Yahoo!|date=10 February 2017}}</ref> He also has [[List of most-followed Instagram accounts|more than 80 million Instagram followers]], the fifth highest for a footballer, behind Cristiano Ronaldo, Messi, [[Neymar]] and [[Kylian Mbappé]], and the second most for a person from the UK, after [[Dua Lipa]].<ref>{{Cite web| url=https://www.trackalytics.com/the-most-followed-instagram-profiles/page/1/| title=The Most Followed Instagram Profiles|website=Trackalytics.com|access-date=17 July 2019|archive-date=1 February 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200201130332/https://www.trackalytics.com/the-most-followed-instagram-profiles/page/1/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://socialblade.com/instagram/top/100/followers|title=Top 100 Instagram Users by Followers- Socialblade Instagram Stats – Instagram Statistics|work=Socialblade|access-date=17 July 2019}}</ref>

During the [[2016 United Kingdom European Union membership referendum|2016 EU referendum]], Beckham voiced his opposition to [[Brexit]], stating: "For our children and their children we should be facing the problems of the world together and not alone. For these reasons, I am voting to remain."<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/voices/as-our-alternative-monarch-surely-david-beckham-backing-remain-will-spark-a-constitutional-crisis-a7093791.html|title=Why David Beckham backing Remain could spark a constitutional crisis|work=The Independent|date=21 June 2016|access-date=27 November 2018}}</ref> Beckham was announced as the new Ambassadorial president of the [[British Fashion Council]] on 11 May 2018.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://news.sky.com/story/david-beckham-appointed-ambassadorial-president-of-british-fashion-council-11367312|title=David Beckham appointed Ambassadorial President of British Fashion Council|publisher=Sky News|access-date=14 May 2018}}</ref> Prior to the June 2018 vote by FIFA member nations for selecting the hosts of the [[2026 FIFA World Cup]], Beckham endorsed the [[United 2026 FIFA World Cup bid|North American bid]] (Canada, Mexico, and the United States).<ref>{{cite news |title=David Beckham: 2026 World Cup in North America would be 'very special. |url=http://www.espn.co.uk/football/blog-fifa/story/3518083/david-beckham-2026-world-cup-in-north-america-would-be-very-special |work=ESPN |date=13 June 2018}}</ref>

Beckham's former club [[LA Galaxy]] unveiled a statue of him outside of their stadium in March 2019, the first of its kind in the [[Major League Soccer|MLS]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/47432089|title=David Beckham: LA Galaxy unveil statue before MLS season opener|date=3 March 2019|access-date=5 March 2019}}</ref> In June 2020, Beckham became a minority owner of the London-based [[esports]] organisation [[Guild Esports]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Seck |first1=Tobias |title=David Beckham Co-Owned Guild Esports Launches, Seeks $31M Investment |url=https://esportsobserver.com/david-beckham-guild-esports/ |access-date=3 April 2021 |work=The Esports Observer |date=25 June 2020 |archive-date=30 March 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210330004137/https://esportsobserver.com/david-beckham-guild-esports/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> In November 2020, [[EA Sports]] had an agreement with Beckham to feature him in ''[[FIFA 21]]'', in which he would earn {{GBP|40M}} from a three-year deal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://en.as.com/en/2020/11/22/football/1606065097_228953.html?omnil=resrelrecom |title=Beckham will earn more from FIFA 2021 than he did at Man Utd and PSG |website=as.com |date=22 November 2020 |access-date=23 November 2020 |archive-date=14 April 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210414030332/https://en.as.com/en/2020/11/22/football/1606065097_228953.html?omnil=resrelrecom |url-status=dead }}</ref> In June 2021, Beckham bought 10% stake of vehicle [[electrification]] firm, Lunaz.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theguardian.com/business/2021/jun/03/david-beckham-buys-stakes-in-vehicle-electrification-firm |title=David Beckham buys stake in vehicle electrification firm |website=The Guardian |date=3 June 2021 }}</ref>

According to [[Sunday Times Rich List 2026|''Sunday Times'' Rich List 2026]], Beckham is the UK's first billionaire sportsman.<ref>{{cite web |title=David Beckham becomes UK's first billionaire sportsman |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/articles/clypx829gwyo |website=BBC Sport |access-date=16 May 2026 |date=15 May 2026}}</ref>

== Philanthropy ==
[[File:"Golden Paws" Paddington Bear, Green Park - geograph.org.uk - 4262168.jpg|thumb|upright|Beckham's England national football team-themed [[Paddington Bear]] statue – "Golden Paws" – in London, auctioned to raise funds for the [[National Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Children|NSPCC]]]]

In 2013, Beckham donated all his {{GBP|3.4M}} salary from Paris Saint-Germain to two children's charities in France.<ref>{{cite web|title=David Beckham finally agrees deal to donate £3.4m PSG wages to French children's charities|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/european/david-beckham-finally-agrees-deal-to-donate-34m-psg-wages-to-french-childrens-charities-8659789.html|work=The Independent|date=14 June 2013}}</ref> He is a founding member of the [[Malaria No More UK]] Leadership Council and helped launch the charity in 2009 with [[Andy Murray]] at Wembley Stadium.<ref>"David Beckham: Fight Malaria by Donating a $10 Bed Net". (25 April 2007). Retrieved 4 May 2009</ref> In November 2014, Beckham designed a [[Paddington Bear]] statue, one of fifty created by various celebrities which were located around London prior to the release of the film ''[[Paddington (film)|Paddington]]''.<ref>{{cite news |title=Why Paddington Bear Statues Have Taken Over London |url=https://www.cntraveler.com/galleries/2014-11-24/paddington-bear-statues-taken-over-london-david-beckham-benedict-cumberbatch |access-date=9 June 2022 |work=Condé Nast}}</ref> The statues were auctioned to raise funds for the [[National Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Children]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Murphy |first=Shaunna |title=Emma Watson Designed A Paddington Bear For Charity And It's Freaking Adorable |url=https://www.mtv.com/news/1984950/emma-watson-paddington-bear/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141107012511/http://www.mtv.com/news/1984950/emma-watson-paddington-bear/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=7 November 2014 |date=3 November 2014 |access-date=9 June 2022 |publisher=MTV}}</ref>

==Appearances in films==
{{Quote box
| width = 24%
| align = right
| quote = "We may be a small country, but we're a great one, too. The country of Shakespeare, Churchill, the Beatles, Sean Connery, Harry Potter. David Beckham's right foot. David Beckham's left foot, come to that."
| source = —[[Hugh Grant]]'s character in ''[[Love Actually]]'' (2003).<ref name="Quote">{{cite news |title=David Beckham in 40 quotes |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/sport/football/babb/11573971/David-Beckham-in-40-quotes.html |work=The Telegraph|date=6 September 2018}}</ref>
}} Beckham never personally appeared in the 2002 film ''[[Bend It Like Beckham]]'', except in archive footage. He and his wife wanted to make cameo appearances, but scheduling proved difficult, so the director used lookalike [[Andy Harmer]] instead.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2002/mar/03/worldcupfootball2002.deniscampbell |title=There's only two David Beckhams|first=Denis|last=Campbell|newspaper=The Guardian|date=3 March 2002}}</ref> 

Beckham makes a cameo appearance with [[Zinedine Zidane]] and [[Raúl (footballer)|Raúl]], in the 2005 film ''[[Goal! (film)|Goal!]]''. Harmer doubled for him in the party scene.<ref>{{cite web|title=Andy Harmer ~ BeckhamLookalike.com|url=http://www.beckhamlookalike.com/clients.htm|work=BeckhamLookalike.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070501102202/http://www.beckhamlookalike.com/clients.htm|archive-date=1 May 2007}}</ref> Beckham himself appears in the sequel, ''[[Goal II: Living the Dream]]'', in a larger role, when the film's lead character gets transferred to Real Madrid.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0473360/ |title=Goal! 2: Living the Dream&nbsp;... |publisher=[[IMDb]] }}</ref> The story centres on the Real Madrid team, with other Madrid players also appearing on and off the pitch, alongside the fictional characters. Through the use of stock footage from the 2006 FIFA World Cup, Beckham appeared in ''[[Goal III: Taking on the World]]'', released [[Direct-to-video|straight to DVD]] on 15 June 2009.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0065743/ |title=David Beckham |website=IMDb |access-date=13 November 2008}}</ref>

In 2013, British magazine ''[[Marketing Week]]'' wrote of Beckham's "somewhat limited acting skills".<ref name="Acting"/> Through his friendship with director [[Guy Ritchie]], he has made two film cameo appearances: as a projectionist in ''[[The Man from U.N.C.L.E. (film)|The Man from U.N.C.L.E.]]'',<ref>{{cite news|title=Guy Ritchie Backs David Beckham As An Actor|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.co.uk/2015/08/07/guy-ritchie-backs-david-beckham-as-actor_n_7957734.html|work=HuffPost|date=24 May 2016}}</ref> and as Trigger in ''[[King Arthur: Legend of the Sword]]''.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.co.uk/entry/david-beckham-king-arthur-charlie-hunnan_uk_5911bd1ae4b0d5d9049fe64b|title=David Beckham's Film Career Takes Another Step With First Clip Of Him In 'King Arthur: Legend Of The Sword'|work=HuffPost|date=9 May 2017}}</ref> Artist [[Sam Taylor-Johnson]] [[David (2004 film)|recorded Beckham sleeping]] in a hotel room in [[Madrid]] in January 2004 following a morning's training session with Real Madrid.<ref name=GuardApr04>{{cite news|last1=Higgins|first1=Charlotte|url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2004/apr/27/arts.artsnews|title=Video portrait captures Beckham asleep|date=27 April 2004|work=[[The Guardian]]|access-date=8 November 2023}}</ref> The film was commissioned by the [[National Portrait Gallery, London|National Portrait Gallery]] in London.<ref name=GuardApr04/>
